pages.note: Pattern here: H2 = threat name; one-sentence lead; two-column table with rows Definition, Example, Trigger (no severity, evidence, or exclusions rows in 3.3). The in-product group is labelled "Azure"; the page title says Entra ID. Catalog-level facts (name, description, default severity, trigger) are assigned here; settings, evidence text, rollup, exclusions, map, and upgrade behavior are in `unplaced` for the later NEW per-threat pages. Impossible Travel File Tag/Process exclusion removal (F316/F046) is not stated on this page; add only if an exclusions line is added. Best page for the threat pattern is this one, extended per threat with severity (default), evidence entry title, and exclusions as F258-F269, F281-F291, F296-F307 supply.

pages.title: Custom Threats

stale.quote: Count –The number of times that an event must occur before a threat is generated
stale.why: Threshold totals the event count (one event can stand for several occurrences) and triggers when the total reaches or exceeds the count.

stale.quote: Group By Perpetrator – When checked, the threat criteria is evaluated on a per-user basis.
stale.why: One threat is created per perpetrator whose total in the window reaches the threshold; events with no perpetrator are ignored in this mode.

stale.quote: **Step 10 –** Click **Save**. The investigation is now saved as a custom threat.
stale.why: A new custom threat, or one whose filters were edited, starts from the current moment and does not evaluate earlier events; editing filters starts a new rollup (F042).

pages.reason: Custom threat evaluation changed (incremental polling, no schedules, rollup per alert query, catch-up limit).
pages.note: Polling/job-service settings (F331, F043, F330) are admin settings and may fit better on a config or troubleshooting page; the Originating Agent filter (F321) is listed as unplaced.
